 Home Physics Branches of physics Quantum field theory
OurBigBook.com Words: 7k Articles: 128
A classical field-theory soliton is a smooth, localized finite-energy solution that behaves as a persistent object. Stability may follow from a topological charge or from a balance among energy terms with different scaling behavior.

Non-topological soliton

Words: 289 Articles: 4
Classical field-theory soliton OurBigBook.com
A non-topological soliton is a localized finite-energy field configuration whose existence or stability is not protected by a nontrivial topological charge. A conserved ordinary Noether charge can instead obstruct its decay. A Q-ball is a standard complex-scalar example: its profile is localized while its phase rotates in time.

Q-ball (ϕ(t,x)=eiωtf(x))

Words: 247 Articles: 3
Non-topological soliton OurBigBook.com
For a complex scalar field with global U(1) invariance and Lagrangian L=21​∣∂t​ϕ∣2−21​∣∇ϕ∣2−U(∣ϕ∣), a Q-ball is a localized phase-rotating configuration with conserved Noether charge Q=∫Im(ϕˉ​ϕt​). At fixed charge its real profile can minimize
EQ​[f]=∫(21​∣∇f∣2+U(f))+2∫f2Q2​.
(1)
Such solutions require a suitable potential and charge range; the complex nature of a field alone does not ensure existence. A common condition is inff>0​2U(f)/f2<U′′(0).

Sextic unique-vacuum Q-ball potential (U(s)=s−s2+s3,s=∣ϕ∣2)

Words: 81
Q-ball OurBigBook.com
This nonnegative potential has its only vacuum at s=0, since U(s)=s[(s−1/2)2+3/4]. For the complex kinetic normalization 21​∣∂ϕ∣2, the small-amplitude mass squared is 2U′(0)=2, whereas mins>0​2U(s)/s=3/2. The radial Q-ball equation has a positive localized profile for frequencies 3/2<ω2<2, for example in three spatial dimensions. It is a standard non-topological soliton potential: the effective profile potential U(f2)−ω2f2/2 is negative somewhere, while its quadratic coefficient near zero is positive. The conserved Noether charge, not vacuum winding, supplies the stabilization mechanism.

Lorentz boost of a Q-ball (E=γM,P=γvM)

Words: 48
Q-ball OurBigBook.com
For a one-dimensional Q-ball, the profile equation gives 21​(f′)2=U(f)−21​ω2f2. Its rest energy is therefore M=∫[(f′)2+ω2f2]. A Lorentz transformation replaces the rest coordinates by τ=γ(t−v(x−x0​)), ξ=γ(x−x0​−vt). The scalar solution eiωτf(ξ) has energy ∫[21​∣ϕt​∣2+21​∣ϕx​∣2+U] and momentum −∫Re(ϕˉ​t​ϕx​). Substitution and dx=dξ/γ give the displayed values and E2−P2=M2.

Charge-constrained scalar-field scaling (EQ​[fλ​]=λ2−dT+λ−dW+λdQ2/(2I))

Words: 59
Q-ball OurBigBook.com
For fλ​(x)=f(λx) in d space dimensions, write T=21​∫∣∇f∣2, W=∫U(f) and I=∫f2. Eliminating the rotation frequency by ω=Q/I gives the displayed fixed-charge scaling. The positive-power charge term can balance the gradient and potential terms even for d≥3. This evades the static Derrick theorem because the field is time-dependent and the relevant variations preserve its Noether charge.

Breather (u(x,t+P)=u(x,t))

Words: 43
Classical field-theory soliton OurBigBook.com
A breather is a spatially localized nonlinear-wave solution periodic in time. It does not separate into independently traveling lumps while it breathes. A Sine-Gordon breather arises from a complex-conjugate soliton pair. In the quantum sine-Gordon model, the associated neutral kink-antikink bound particles are also called breathers.

Semiclassical soliton mass (M=Mcl​+ΔM1loop​+⋯)

Words: 230 Articles: 3
Classical field-theory soliton OurBigBook.com
A weak-coupling expansion of a vacuum-subtracted soliton mass begins with the classical energy and adds the Gaussian fluctuation approximation. For Sine-Gordon theory, M=8m/β2+ΔM1loop​+O(mβ2). The term of order m includes both the vacuum-subtracted fluctuation frequencies and the appropriate mass counterterm.

One-loop soliton mass correction (ΔMosc​=21​∑n​(Ωn​−Ωn(0)​))

Words: 196 Articles: 2
Semiclassical soliton mass OurBigBook.com
In a common finite-volume regularization in quantum field theory, the oscillator contribution is ΔMosc​=21​∑n​(Ωn​−Ωn(0)​), including every discrete and continuum-derived mode and treating translation as a collective coordinate. Physical frequencies are Ωn​=mωn​ when coordinates are measured in units of m−1. A mass counterterm is added only afterwards. The vacuum subtraction removes the extensive vacuum energy but can leave an ultraviolet divergence.

Mode-number regularization of soliton masses

Words: 142 Articles: 1
One-loop soliton mass correction OurBigBook.com
Compare the same total number of finite-box modes in the soliton and vacuum sectors before removing the ultraviolet cutoff. A localized bound state replaces a continuum mode, and its contribution must be retained. For the Sine-Gordon kink fluctuation operator and the odd phase branch δ(k)=2arctan(1/k), the bound translation mode replaces the free k=0 oscillator. Thus the complete oscillator correction is −m/2−(m/2)∫dkδ(k)k/[2πk2+1​] in this convention. The continuum integral alone misses the finite −m/2 contribution.
Cutoff surface term for a Sine-Gordon kink (−ω(Λ)δ(Λ)/(2π)⟶−m/π)
Words: 75
Mode-number regularization of soliton masses OurBigBook.com
The scattering phase shift δ(k)=2arctan(m/k) of the Sine-Gordon kink fluctuation operator gives a continuum frequency sum. In mode-number regularization of soliton masses, the zero-frequency translation mode replaces the vacuum oscillator at k=0. The bare difference is −m/2−(2π)−1∫0Λ​δ(k)k/k2+m2​dk. Integration by parts cancels the lower endpoint against −m/2 and produces the displayed upper surface term. Although δ(Λ) vanishes, its product with ω(Λ) tends to 2m. Vacuum normal ordering cancels the logarithmic bulk ultraviolet divergence, leaving this finite one-loop soliton mass correction. Parameters and finite counterterms must be fixed by a stated renormalization condition.

Vacuum-subtracted soliton mass (M=EQ=1​−EQ=0​)

Words: 50
Classical field-theory soliton OurBigBook.com
The rest mass of a stable soliton is the lowest energy in its topological sector minus the vacuum energy, in the infinite-volume limit. If Euclidean kernels KQ​(τ) have nonzero overlap with the sector's lowest-energy states, then M=−limτ→∞​τ−1log[K1​(τ)/K0​(τ)], followed by the infinite-volume limit. A Euclidean path integral represents these kernels, with boundary wavefunctionals included if necessary.

Soliton time delay (Δt=−Δx/v)

Words: 168 Articles: 2
Classical field-theory soliton OurBigBook.com
If a labeled soliton approaches x=vt+a−​ before a collision and x=vt+a+​ afterwards, its spatial shift is Δx=a+​−a−​. For v=0, define its time delay at a fixed spatial point by Δt=−Δx/v. Thus a positive forward shift of a right-moving soliton is a negative time delay. For a stationary soliton, the spatial shift is well defined but this time-delay definition is not.

Full S-matrix phase from a classical soliton delay (dδ/dE=ΔT/ℏ,S=eiδ)

Words: 50
Soliton time delay OurBigBook.com
A narrow outgoing energy packet has phase −ET/ℏ+δ(E), so stationary phase gives the arrival shift ΔT=ℏδ′(E). For two equal-mass solitons with relative rapidity θ, E=2Mcosh(θ/2). The convention S=e2iδpw​ instead gives 2ℏδpw′​=ΔT. Classical time delays determine only the energy-dependent phase difference, not its constant branch.

Pairwise additivity of soliton shifts (Δxi​=∑j=i​Δxi∣j​)

Words: 54
Soliton time delay OurBigBook.com
A many-soliton spatial shift is pairwise additive when Δxi​=∑j=i​Δxi∣j​. In the all-kink sector of Sine-Gordon theory, Δxi∣j​=−sgn(vi​−vj​)logtanh2[(θi​−θj​)/2]/coshθi​. Dominant spectator exponentials in the Sine-Gordon multisoliton tau representation multiply the effective exponential of kink i, so their logarithms add. This is a classical signature of factorized scattering, with no independent many-body contribution to the asymptotic shift.

Finite-energy field configuration (E[Φ]<∞)

Words: 146 Articles: 1
Classical field-theory soliton OurBigBook.com
A finite-energy field configuration has integrable energy density after the vacuum energy has been subtracted. The boundary conditions used for a localized classical field-theory soliton require approaching a vacuum at spatial infinity. In one dimension the two ends may approach distinct scalar-field vacua; in a gauge theory the asymptotic field can have nontrivial winding even when its local energy density tends to zero.

Finite sigma-model energy need not give a limit at infinity

Finite-energy field configuration OurBigBook.com
For arbitrary maps ϕ:R2→S2, integrability of the Dirichlet energy does not imply continuous extension to the one-point compactification. For large r, take
ϕ(r,ϑ)=(sina(r),0,cosa(r)),a(r)=loglogr,
(2)
and interpolate smoothly to a constant on a bounded disk. Its exterior energy is
21​∫∣x∣≥R​∣∇ϕ∣2d2x=π∫R∞​rlog2rdr​=logRπ​<∞.
(3)
The field has no limit because a(r) keeps winding. A continuous extension at the point at infinity instead requires ϕ(x)→ϕ∞​ uniformly outside sufficiently large disks. This fixed-limit boundary condition is standard for a sigma-model lump, but is extra information beyond finite energy for arbitrary fields.

Collective coordinate of a soliton (qa(t))

Words: 374 Articles: 6
Classical field-theory soliton OurBigBook.com
A collective coordinate parametrizes a family of static classical field-theory solitons, for example their position or internal orientation. Derivatives with respect to these parameters are zero modes in field theory when the family has constant energy. Slowly varying coordinates describe low-energy motion, provided the excluded modes and radiation are negligible; gauge variations must first be removed in a gauge-theory soliton.

Quantization of a periodic soliton coordinate (α0​∼α0​+2π⟹pα0​​∈ℏZ)

Words: 38
Collective coordinate of a soliton OurBigBook.com
The conjugate momentum to a periodic internal soliton angle generates shifts of that angle. Single-valued wavefunctions, or Bohr-Sommerfeld quantization with zero Maslov index, quantize this canonical momentum. A theta term can shift the relation between canonical momentum and mechanical charge without changing integer canonical labels.

Collective-coordinate effective Lagrangian for a soliton

Collective coordinate of a soliton OurBigBook.com
A collective-coordinate approximation substitutes a finite-parameter soliton ansatz into the field action and integrates over space. Its Euler-Lagrange equations approximate the slow motion of the soliton parameters.

Collective-coordinate effective Lagrangian for a soliton OurBigBook.com
Substitute the instantaneous Sine-Gordon kink profile θK​(γ(x−X)) and prescribed velocity −γX˙θK′​ with γ=(1−X˙2)−1/2 into the field density. For A1​=0, A0​=xf(t), the integrals ∫(θK′​)2=8 and ∫θK′​=2π give the displayed collective-coordinate effective Lagrangian. Its equation is d(8γX˙)/dt=−2πf. This is relativistic particle motion with mass 8 and topological coupling charge 2π. Instantaneous-boost effective action for a sine-Gordon kink OurBigBook.com
The actual derivative of θK​(γ(t)(x−X(t))) is [γ˙​(x−X)−γX˙]θK′​. The omitted contribution is first order in acceleration. Its cross term with the translation velocity integrates to zero because ∫y(θK′​(y))2dy=0. The square adds γ˙​2∫y2(θK′​)2dy/(2γ3)=π2γ˙​2/(3γ3) to the spatially integrated density, since θK′​=2sechy and ∫y2(θK′​)2dy=2π2/3. Moduli-space approximation for solitons (Leff​=21​gab​(q)q˙​aq˙​b−E0​)

Words: 126 Articles: 1
Collective coordinate of a soliton OurBigBook.com
Substitute a static soliton family with slowly time-dependent collective coordinates into the action. The kinetic energy induces a Riemannian metric g on the family, after imposing any Gauss law constraint in gauge theory constraint and projecting out gauge directions. If its static energy is constant, the Euler-Lagrange equations are the geodesic equations of g. An approximately flat family instead carries a potential V(q). This approximation neglects excitations of the other field modes and is justified only when their effects are small on the time and energy scales studied.

Collective-coordinate quantization (H=−ℏ2Δg​/2+V)

Words: 49
Moduli-space approximation for solitons OurBigBook.com
Quantizing a moduli-space approximation gives wavefunctions with measure detg​ddq and, under the minimal scalar ordering, the Hamiltonian operator −ℏ2Δg​/2+V, where Δg​ is the Laplace-Beltrami operator. Global identifications, statistics and regularity supply additional restrictions on wavefunctions. Curvature-dependent ordering terms or quantum corrections are extra choices, not determined by the classical kinetic energy alone.

Topological charge (Q)

Words: 296 Articles: 5
Classical field-theory soliton OurBigBook.com
A topological charge is an integer or other discrete invariant determined by the homotopy class or characteristic class of a field configuration. Continuous finite-energy deformations cannot change it without crossing a singular or forbidden configuration.

Vacuum-boundary degree as a defect charge (Q=deg(Sd−1→Sd−1))

Words: 49
Topological charge OurBigBook.com
A normalized vacuum field on a sphere surrounding a core can define Sd−1→Sd−1 with integer topological degree. Nonzero degree obstructs its extension through the enclosed ball while staying in the vacuum manifold. This accounts for the winding number of a vortex and the spherical degree of a magnetic monopole, with the appropriate vacuum targets.

Degree and energetic stability of a field configuration (E2​(R)∝R,E4​(R)∝R−1)

Words: 60
Topological charge OurBigBook.com
A nonzero topological degree obstructs smooth unwinding with fixed boundary data, but does not by itself give a stable finite size. In three dimensions a two-derivative energy scales as R and can decrease as a configuration shrinks at fixed degree. The four-derivative Skyrme term scales as R−1 and can balance this tendency. Derrick theorem addresses the energetic issue; a singular limiting configuration can evade smooth homotopy conservation.

Topological current (∂μ​jtopμ​=0)

Words: 109 Articles: 1
Topological charge OurBigBook.com
A local current whose conservation follows from field geometry rather than requiring the field equation. For Skyrmions, pulling back the closed volume form on the target three-sphere gives the current associated with topological baryon number in the Skyrme model. Its spatial integral is a topological charge, unchanged by smooth evolution with the prescribed boundary behaviour.

Pullback-volume representation of a topological current (d(ϕ∗ω)=0,Q=∫space​ϕ∗ω)

Words: 61
Topological current OurBigBook.com
A closed target d-form ω pulls back under a spacetime field ϕ to a closed form α=ϕ∗ω. Its dual defines an identically conserved topological current. For a compact oriented spatial d-manifold and an equally dimensional oriented target with ∫ω=1, the spatial integral is the topological degree. Conservation follows without the field equations; changing boundary flux can change the charge.

Topological sector ([Φ])

Words: 43
Topological charge OurBigBook.com
A connected component, or homotopy class, of admissible field configurations with fixed asymptotic conditions. Distinct topological sectors cannot be joined by a continuous deformation within that configuration space. A nonzero topological charge labels a sector, but a stable finite-size energy minimum also depends on the energy functional.

Derrick's theorem

Words: 301 Articles: 5
Classical field-theory soliton OurBigBook.com
Derrick's scaling argument tests a static field configuration by rescaling space. A soliton can be stationary only if energy terms with opposite scaling powers balance at the original scale.

Two-dimensional flat-target Derrick obstruction

Words: 99
Derrick's theorem OurBigBook.com
For smooth fields into Rl with nonnegative differentiable potential and finite energy, Derrick scaling in two spatial dimensions forces the potential integral to vanish. Thus the field takes values where U=0 and ∇U=0, so its static field equation makes every component harmonic. Each first derivative is an entire harmonic function in L2 space; the mean-value inequality on arbitrarily large balls forces it to vanish. Hence the field is constant. The scale identity alone does not exclude a pure-gradient model; this additional argument uses the flat unconstrained target. Curved-target harmonic maps, for example the O3 nonlinear sigma model, can instead have finite-energy nonconstant solutions.

Derrick scaling (ϕλ​(x)=ϕ(λx))

Words: 150 Articles: 2
Derrick's theorem OurBigBook.com
Under Derrick scaling, an energy term containing m spatial derivatives and homogeneous of degree m in those derivatives scales as λm−D in D spatial dimensions.

No static finite-energy lump in three-dimensional pure Yang-Mills theory (E[A(s)]=sE[A])

Words: 71
Derrick scaling OurBigBook.com
For a smooth gauge field on R3 with finite positive magnetic energy, dilate its connection one-form by Ai(s)​(x)=sAi​(sx). Its gauge curvature scales as Fij(s)​(x)=s2Fij​(sx), so the energy scales as s4s−3E=sE. A static stationary configuration must have zero derivative at s=1, forcing E=0 and hence F=0. This Derrick scaling argument assumes the dilation preserves the boundary conditions and that boundary terms vanish. It does not exclude four-dimensional Yang-Mills instantons, whose Euclidean action is scale invariant.

Finite Yang-Mills action forbids nontrivial translation symmetry

Words: 95
Yang-Mills instanton OurBigBook.com
A smooth gauge field of finite positive Euclidean Yang-Mills action cannot be invariant under a nonzero translation, even up to gauge transformation. The positive gauge-invariant action density would be periodic along that translation. A ball on which the density is bounded below by a positive constant has infinitely many disjoint translated copies, making the action infinite. Continuous translation invariance is a special case. Consequently a nonflat translation-invariant field satisfying the Anti-self-dual Yang-Mills equations on R3×R is not a finite-action Yang-Mills instanton. Flat connections are the zero-action exception. Translations still act on instanton moduli, sending a localized instanton to a distinct centered configuration.

Skyrme model

Words: 1k Articles: 20
Classical field-theory soliton OurBigBook.com
The Skyrme model is a nonlinear sigma model for an SU(2)-valued field supplemented by a four-derivative term that evades Derrick collapse. Its topological degree is baryon number, and finite-energy solitons are Skyrmions.

Derrick dimension test for the Skyrme model (E(L)=Ld−2E2​+Ld−4E4​)

Words: 156 Articles: 1
Skyrme model OurBigBook.com
For a spatially dilated Skyrme model field UL​(x)=U(x/L), the quadratic and quartic derivative energies scale as shown. A static stationary field must satisfy (d−2)E2​+(d−4)E4​=0. In three spatial dimensions this permits E2​=E4​ and a positive second variation along scale. In two dimensions it requires E4​=0, and in four or more it forces a constant finite-energy smooth field. In one dimension the commutator term vanishes identically. Derrick scaling tests a necessary variational condition, not existence or stability under all deformations.

Commuting-current obstruction in a two-dimensional Skyrme model ([R1​,R2​]=0,∂i​Ri​=0 ⟹ Ri​=0)

Derrick dimension test for the Skyrme model OurBigBook.com
For a smooth finite-energy static planar Skyrme model field, Derrick scaling gives zero quartic energy, hence [R1​,R2​]=0 pointwise. The quartic first variation then vanishes, leaving the sigma-model equation ∂i​Ri​=0. The right-current Maurer-Cartan equation gives ∂1​R2​−∂2​R1​=[R1​,R2​]=0. Each current component is therefore harmonic on the plane and square-integrable. The mean-value estimate on expanding disks makes each component zero, so U is constant. This excludes smooth finite-energy planar static solutions of this potential-free SU(2) model, without misapplying the same conclusion to a pure curved-target sigma model.

Skyrme model OurBigBook.com
The particular quartic-derivative interaction in the Skyrme model, with Lμ​=U†∂μ​U. Its static energy is positive and scales inversely with soliton size, opposing collapse under Derrick scaling. It is one choice of four-derivative mesonic interaction, not the whole general fourth-order chiral perturbation theory Lagrangian.

Vacuum-preserving symmetry of the Skyrme model (L=R)

Words: 97
Skyrme model OurBigBook.com
The massless derivative Skyrme model has chiral symmetry U↦LUR†. For the fixed finite-energy boundary condition U(∞)=1, a transformation preserves the same vacuum exactly when LR†=1, or L=R. This leaves conjugation U↦AUA†, the isospin action. Since A and −A act identically, its effective group is SO(3). Together with spatial translations and rotations it generates the localized zero-mode orbit of a Skyrmion. Independent axial rotations change the massless vacuum and are not additional normalizable rigid orientation modes in that fixed-vacuum sector. A usual positive pion-mass term preserves only conjugation even before the boundary condition is imposed.

Skyrmion

Words: 1k Articles: 15
Skyrme model OurBigBook.com
A Skyrmion is a finite-energy topological soliton of the Skyrme model. Its baryon number is the degree of the compactified spatial map S3→SU(2)≃S3.

Skyrmion model of a nucleus (B=A)

Words: 45
Skyrmion OurBigBook.com
A charge-A multi-Skyrmion provides an intrinsic field configuration for an atomic nucleus with mass number A. Its spatial and isospin collective coordinates must be quantized, with Finkelstein-Rubinstein constraints, before assigning physical nuclear states. A classical intrinsic shape is distinct from rotationally invariant observables in a spin-zero state.

Skyrmion stabilizer and collective-coordinate orbit (O=G/H)

Words: 99
Skyrmion OurBigBook.com
For a centered static Skyrmion U0​, the effective rotation-isorotation group is G=SO(3)space​×SO(3)iso​. Its stabilizer subgroup H consists of pairs obeying AU0​(R−1x)A†=U0​(x). Thus distinct rigid orientations form the homogeneous space G/H, by the orbit-stabilizer theorem. The unit hedgehog has diagonal SO(3) stabilizer and three orientation coordinates; the toroidal two-Skyrmion has a one-dimensional continuous stabilizer and five; the tetrahedral and cubic cases have discrete stabilizers and six. Adding three translations gives zero-mode orbit dimensions 6, 8, 9, 9. These are symmetry-generated low-energy coordinates, not a claim that non-Bogomolny multi-Skyrmion solutions possess an exact flat moduli space of arbitrary separations.

Cubic four-Skyrmion (B=4)

Words: 77
Skyrmion OurBigBook.com
The familiar low-energy B=4 Skyrmion has a cubic baryon-density shell with six face-hole directions and full density symmetry Oh​, the symmetry group of a cube. The proper subgroup is O≅S4​, the rotational symmetry group of a cube; its field invariance includes compensating isorotations. A useful rational map approximation for Skyrmions has R(z)=(z4+2i3​z2+1)/(z4−2i3​z2+1). The relation R(iz)=1/R(z) pairs a spatial quarter-turn with a target half-turn. Its branch directions are z=0,∞,±1,±i, corresponding to the six coordinate-axis directions. The map gives an approximate field, not an exact analytic energy-minimizing solution.

Tetrahedral three-Skyrmion (B=3)

Words: 75
Skyrmion OurBigBook.com
The familiar low-energy B=3 Skyrmion has tetrahedral baryon-density symmetry Td​. Proper rotations form the tetrahedral symmetry group T≅A4​, acting on the field with compensating isorotations. An angular approximation is R(z)=(i3​z2−1)/(z3−i3​z). Its Wronskian of a rational map is proportional to z4+2i3​z2+1. The four branch directions are the face-hole directions of a tetrahedral shell. A rational map and a variational radial profile approximate the actual field, and baryon-density symmetry must be distinguished from invariance of the pion field under an unaccompanied spatial rotation.

The angular ansatz R(z)=z2 in the rational map approximation for Skyrmions explains the axial relation R(eiθz)=e2iθR(z): spatial rotation through θ is accompanied by isorotation through 2θ. The angular density vanishes at the two axial directions, yielding the toroidal hole. This describes the familiar minimal branch and a useful approximate field; it is not an assertion that every degree-two field is toroidal.

Finkelstein-Rubinstein constraints

Words: 193 Articles: 1
Skyrmion OurBigBook.com
Finkelstein-Rubinstein constraints impose the allowed signs under combined spatial and isospin rotations of a quantized Skyrmion. They encode the fermionic or bosonic exchange behavior of topological solitons.
Collective-rotation constraints for a Skyrmion (DJ(R)DI(A)Ψ=χFR​Ψ)
Words: 166
Finkelstein-Rubinstein constraints OurBigBook.com
A rigid Skyrmion orientation is quantized on a cover of its Skyrmion collective-coordinate orbit. A lifted combined rotation in the static field's stabilizer subgroup identifies the same classical field and imposes DJ(R)DI(A)Ψ=χFR​Ψ, where the sign is the chosen Finkelstein-Rubinstein constraints character of that configuration-space loop. Choosing the nontrivial character models unit baryons as fermions. A 2π spatial rotation or isorotation of charge B then has sign (−1)B: deforming the field to separated unit lumps adds the unit-lump loop classes in the fundamental group Z2​, while the labelled orbital paths can be contracted in three dimensions. The resulting Finkelstein-Rubinstein constraints sign is the product of the unit-lump signs. Hence spin and isospin are half-integer for odd B and integer for even B. Further stabilizer constraints restrict which pairs (J,I) and which body-fixed states occur. The energy operator comes from the inertia tensors on the orbit; symmetry selects allowed states but does not by itself determine their energies. A bosonic choice of the trivial topological character is mathematically possible but does not model a fermionic nucleon.
